title: Bounds that change the prior — lognormal(2, 1) cut at 1
title_pt: Limites que mudam a priori — lognormal(2, 1) cortada em 1
note: The air-conditioning data again, with the prior an old hand-written model used: lognormal(2, 1) on the rate, with the rate bounded to [0, 1]. The bound keeps 2.3% of the prior's mass and moves its median from 7.4 to 0.76, so the prior in force is not the one written down; the Model tab plots the truncated density and warns. Even with 12 failures it still matters: against the first example the rate comes out about 50% higher (mean time to failure 75 h instead of 116 h, R(100 h) 0.26 instead of 0.41), because what is left of the prior piles up near the bound at 1.
note_pt: De novo os dados do ar-condicionado, com a priori que um modelo antigo escrito à mão usava: lognormal(2, 1) na taxa, com a taxa limitada a [0, 1]. O limite mantém 2,3% da massa da priori e leva a mediana de 7,4 para 0,76: a priori em vigor não é a que foi escrita, e a aba Model mostra a densidade truncada e avisa. Mesmo com 12 falhas isso pesa: comparada ao primeiro exemplo, a taxa sai cerca de 50% maior (tempo médio até a falha de 75 h em vez de 116 h, R(100 h) de 0,26 em vez de 0,41), porque o que sobra da priori se acumula perto do limite 1.
source: Proschan, F. (1963). Theoretical explanation of observed decreasing failure rate. Technometrics 5(3), 375-383. The 12 intervals are the `aircondit` data of Davison and Hinkley (1997), Bootstrap Methods and their Application (R package boot).
source_pt: Proschan, F. (1963). Theoretical explanation of observed decreasing failure rate. Technometrics 5(3), 375-383. Os 12 intervalos são os dados `aircondit` de Davison e Hinkley (1997), Bootstrap Methods and their Application (pacote R boot).
